title: Positive part equals half the total variation of the density
statement:
Let $\mu$ and $
u$ be probability measures on a measurable space $\Omega$, with $\mu$ absolutely continuous with respect to $
u$, and write $ rac{d\mu}{d
u}$ for the Radon–Nikodym density of $\mu$ with respect to $
u$. Then the excess mass of the density above $1$, integrated over the region where the density is at least $1$, equals half the $L^1(
u)$-distance of the density from $1$:
\[
\int_{\{x\,:\, rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)\,\ge\,1\}} \left( rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)-1ight)\,d
u(x) \;=\;  rac{1}{2}\int_{\Omega} \left| rac{d\mu}{d
u}(x)-1ight|\,d
u(x).
\]
hypotheses_covered: μ and ν are probability measures on a measurable space Ω
μ is absolutely continuous with respect to ν
